A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same S2-Guidance work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original Gaussian-mixture and CIFAR-10 experiments, image/video generation benchmarks, Flux evaluation, and a 14-participant user study in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds ImageNet evaluation, block-dropping analyses, computational measurements, and quantitative stochastic-variance results.

M1.justification: In Equations 3–4 and Algorithm 1, v1 subtracts the raw sub-network prediction, whereas v3 subtracts its deviation from the full conditional prediction: CFG - omega*(D_sub-D_cond). This substantially changes the specified inference correction. However, v3's Appendix A still derives the earlier rule, leaving its implementation alignment unresolved.

E1.justification: v3 adds class-conditional ImageNet 256x256 generation as a full benchmark evaluation, substantially extending coverage beyond v1's Gaussian/CIFAR-10 demonstrations and text-conditioned generation benchmarks. HPSv2.1, T2I-CompBench, VBench, and the existing Flux evaluation remain.

E2.justification: v3 adds SEG to both SD3 and SD3.5 comparisons in Table 1 and evaluates ADG in the new ImageNet comparison in Table 2. Existing VBench and user-study comparator sets remain unchanged. The additional higher-budget CFG row is a protocol change, not a new method.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include SiT-XL ImageNet evaluation using IS/FID, fixed-block and application-interval controls on SiT/DiT, a 28-step resource benchmark, and comparisons using increased CFG computation and varying inference budgets. Existing T2I/T2V guidance settings and the user-study protocol are retained.

E4.justification: Section 4.5 and Appendix B.2 add analyses of block identity and dropping intervals, a 28-block visual stress test, computational cost and memory, performance under comparable computational budgets, and stochastic stability. Existing guidance-scale, drop-ratio, and single-versus-multiple-subnetwork analyses remain.

E5.justification: New Table 7 reports variance, standard deviation, and coefficient of variation across stochastic-dropping repetitions with initial noise fixed. v1 contained qualitative comparisons across seeds but no corresponding quantitative uncertainty report. v3 does not specify the repetition count or add uncertainty estimates throughout the benchmark tables.

E6.justification: Most existing benchmark values are retained, while ImageNet, SEG, computational-control, resource, and stability results are added. SEG now exceeds S2-Guidance on SD3.5 shape and texture scores: 55.52 versus 51.23 and 54.03 versus 50.13. ImageNet Table 2 reports IS 259.12 and FID 2.03 for S2-Guidance, but Section 4.2 inconsistently states 259.22 and 2.08.

T1.justification: Appendix A.2 replaces v1's approximate, explicitly non-proof unbiasedness argument with a defined population target and exact Monte Carlo expectation identities. Appendix A.1.2 also distinguishes the posterior mean from its estimator. Most Bayesian derivation remains unchanged and is not reconciled with the revised main-text guidance equations.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions explicitly extend the claimed empirical scope to class-conditional ImageNet generation. The introduction qualifies computational savings as relative to the naive variant, and the conclusion describes diffusion transformers specifically. The central training-free self-guidance and superiority claims remain.

C2.justification: v3 newly acknowledges approximately 40% computational overhead and explains unchanged peak memory through sequential evaluations. It adds interpretations of architecture-dependent block importance and stochastic stability, strengthens the temporal-integration rationale, and discusses possible applications beyond DiT in Appendix C. These substantially expand practical tradeoffs and applicability discussion.

D1.justification: v3 newly documents preservation of structurally important blocks, sequential full-model/sub-network evaluations, and runtime, FLOP, and memory measurements. Appendix B.4's guidance hyperparameters, H20 hardware, and baseline implementation information remain unchanged. Both versions retain the same project address and promise future code release.

R1.justification: v3 expands the Bayesian discussion with ensemble literature, including Deep Ensembles, Snapshot Ensembles, and BatchEnsemble. New Appendix C establishes a much broader set of connections to editing, preference alignment, video consistency, robustness, and prospective LLM/MLLM applications. The central positioning against CFG and Autoguidance remains.

P1.justification: Parts of the abstract, introduction, background, and experimental discussion are rewritten or condensed; terminology, title, author information, and publication header are updated. ImageNet and future-work sections are inserted, but the overall narrative and much of the appendix prose retain v1's structure.

P2.justification: Figure 7 expands from two to five panels; v3 adds ImageNet, resource, and variance tables plus Figures 14–15. Figure 2 and Algorithm 1 become smaller displays with surrounding text. The iteration half of v1's Table 3 is removed while its related Figure 8 remains. Most earlier qualitative figures are reused.

improvement.justification: The added ImageNet, block-dropping, computational-budget, and stability evaluations strengthen empirical scrutiny. However, v3 changes its central guidance rule without reconciling Appendix A's derivation, leaving uncertainty about which procedure supports the results. The new ImageNet table also conflicts with its accompanying prose, while SEG results qualify retained superiority claims. These substantive reporting problems prevent a confident net quality judgment.
